summary: iter-292 backend regression for Straumann BLT (Bone Level Tapered) implant systems — ALL 24 tests PASS. Verified: 3 new BLT systems present with correct counts (Roxolid SLActive=24, Roxolid SLA=21, Ti SLA=18) and Ø lists [2.9/3.3/4.1/4.8 for Roxolid; 3.3/4.1/4.8 for Ti]; legacy ('Straumann','BLT') 4-row stub is removed; total Straumann library = exactly 7 systems (3 BLT + 4 BLX); /api/drilling-protocols/available exposes the 3 BLT systems; POST /generate for each BLT system on D1+D4 returns protocol_type containing 'Straumann BLT', steps >=6 with strict schema {step,drill_type,code,diameter,depth,cortical_only,rpm,irrigation,note}; D1 includes Profile+Tap, D4 excludes Tap and has no cortical_only Profile; invalid Ø6.5/L15 returns graceful (200 with no full protocol, not 500); BLX (4)/Adin (8)/Alpha Bio (8) brand counts intact; BLX Roxolid SLActive Ø4.0 L10 D2 and Adin Touareg-S Ø4.2 L10 D2 still generate correctly.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 14,937 lines — far exceeds 700-line guideline. The drilling-protocol dispatcher (12613-12790) is a deeply nested if/elif chain across 15+ protocol families. Strongly recommend extracting each family into its own dispatcher module (one per brand) with a registry pattern, similar to how straumann_blt_data.py, straumann_blx_data.py and adin_data.py are already isolated as data modules.

Generator returns an empty list [] for invalid Ø (e.g. Ø6.5) — endpoint then 200s with a body containing a single 'Implant Placement' seat step. Strictly per the request, an explicit 400/404 with a graceful message would be more correct than a 200-with-stub. Currently passes the 'not 500' bar, but consider raising HTTPException(400, 'Diameter Ø{d} not available in {system}') when generate_blt_protocol returns []. Same shortcoming likely exists in BLX and others.
Long ternary chain at server.py:12752 for insertion_torque is unreadable — flatten into a dict lookup keyed by protocol_family.

Drilling-protocols/available endpoint shape was not visible in the request files; tests handle both list-of-dict and list-of-string variants. Recommend a typed Pydantic response model for consistency.
